newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Wednesday January 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Wednesday January 15.

text.p: The following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Centre-right Freedom Alliance leaders decide to vote with the government on a plan to redraft Italy's constitution. Opposition leader Silvio Berlusconi said the Freedom Alliance is not divided and added "If it doesn't work we go out" (all).
* Italian state railways said there appeared to be nothing wrong with the high-speed train "Pendolino" that derailed at the weekend killing eight people (all).
* The government presented a draft reform of Italy's school system which would make education compulsory from 5 to 15 years (all).
* A committal hearing is scheduled today to examine a prosecutor's bid to try Prime Minister Romano Prodi for alleged abuse of office and conflict of interest (all).

* After six days of strong gains, Italian shares paused but then resumed their rally with the all-share Mibtel index rising 3.46 percent. Italian bond futures scaled a new record high of 130.83 on the LIFFE March contract (all).

* Metalworkers's unions accuse employers association Federmeccanica of provocation after it again rejected a government arbitration proposal for contract renewal. Tension also rose as a committee from industrial association Confindustria proposed a delay by 12 months in the application of working contracts in southern Italy (all).

* In an interview, Communist Refoundation party leader Fausto Bertinotti says he does not see any need for an additional mini-budget this year and adds "I do rule out any government intervention on health and pensions this year" (La Stampa).
* The government is reported to be considering a "superbudget" law for 1998 and 1999 in June this year (Corriere della Sera).

* In an interview, Gianmario Rossignolo, chairman of white goods company Zanussi, says talks are underway for the sale of information technology group Olivetti's ailing PC division. An announcement will be made today or tomorrow (Il Sole 24 Ore).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
